**What the simulations show** (synthetic example — authored characterization, no experimental measurements):

- All twelve pairs reach 100% dried, in 6.00 h (0.2 Torr / 10 °C) to 34.58 h (0.2 Torr / −25 °C).
- **Thermal constraint (vial-bottom ≤ −36.0 °C): every pair fails.** The coldest is 0.05 Torr / −25 °C, whose maximum returned vial-bottom temperature is −32.55 °C — 3.45 °C above the limit. In that run the bottom crosses −36.0 °C between returned nodes at 4.0 h (−36.88 °C, 22.3% dried) and 7.0 h (−35.59 °C, 36.8% dried), i.e. mid-sublimation, so this is not an end-of-run tail. The warmest is 0.2 Torr / 10 °C at −17.00 °C (19.0 °C over).
- **Equipment line (whole-batch rate vs −0.182 + 11.7·P kg/h):** batch rate = peak flux × 5.024 m² (16,000 vials × 3.14 cm², derived). Line values: 0.403 kg/h at 0.05 Torr, 0.988 at 0.1 Torr, 2.158 at 0.2 Torr. Only **0.2 Torr / −25 °C** fits (peak 0.986 kg/h, 1.172 kg/h headroom); 0.2 Torr / −15 °C misses by 0.002 kg/h (2.160 vs 2.158 — at the line within solver precision); all others exceed by ~0.9–4.3 kg/h.
- The one equipment-feasible pair (0.2 Torr / −25 °C, 34.58 h) exceeds the critical temperature by 7.10 °C. So no recipe is selected, and no predicted time or achieved margins are recorded; the per-pair exceedances above are simple derived arithmetic on returned simulator outputs.

**What I could not check:** temperatures between solver nodes (the native model gives no continuous-maximum guarantee, so both constraints were checked only at returned nodes); any shelf/pressure pair outside the twelve allowed; and I did not verify the vial count, vial area, or the equipment-line coefficients against site equipment or CMMS records — I used them exactly as stated in the characterization source, per your instruction. Nothing here is a measured outcome, an equipment operation, or an approval.
